summary: postinstall fetches remote JSON and dispatches an attacker-chosen global with attacker-supplied argument
details: croft-node 1.1.2 declares a postinstall lifecycle script that runs dist/config.js on npm install. That script performs an outbound HTTPS fetch to https://my-api.trade-api.workers.dev?id=1 and evaluates the JSON response as `globalThis[data.success](data.id)` — the remote endpoint controls both which global is invoked (e.g. eval, require, Function) and the argument passed to it. This is a remote-controlled code-execution primitive that fires automatically on `npm install`. The same file also contains a top-level `globalThis[tag](text)` reference to identifiers not defined in the file, consistent with an obfuscated stager sink. The package's stated purpose (an in-memory keyed store) has no legitimate need for network I/O at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
